title: Trace Details Canvas: contextual summary, cross-request linker, and smart filters
creator: Lina Morales
description: Design a consolidated Trace Details Canvas for Redwood Console that replaces the current multi-panel layout with a single adaptive surface focused on rapid root-cause workflows. Key goals: surface a compact contextual summary for the selected request, enable frictionless navigation to related requests via a cross-request linker, and introduce smart, composable filters (time, tag, status, correlation-id membership) that highlight and sample traces for efficient investigation. This ticket covers the interactive prototype, accessibility considerations, and design handoff artifacts for engineering implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Contextual Summary card implemented at top of canvas showing request metadata (timestamp, model, route, latency, token counts) and quick actions (open logs, open metrics, copy correlation ID)
Waterfall timeline is horizontally scrollable with lane grouping, minimap and a frame scrubber that syncs with a span detail panel
Cross-Request Linker surfaces up to 10 related requests (same correlation ID or topological neighbors) and allows inline preview without leaving the canvas
Smart Filters support multi-select predicates, AND/OR composition, and a sample toggle that highlights representative traces when result size > 200
Prototype annotated for behavior: collapsing long KV payloads, lazy-loading span timelines, non-blocking rendering of large spans
Design tokens, margins, and color usage documented for engineering handoff; accessibility contrast and keyboard navigation covered
UX review feedback addressed (see comments) and a final Figma file shared in attachments
design_notes: We moved from a three-column layout to a single canvas with collapsible rails to reduce context switching during investigations.

Contextual Summary is intentionally compact and prioritizes quick actions: Copy Correlation ID, Open Logs (splits to logs view), Open Metrics (links to dashboard), and Create Incident (links to incident workflow).

Cross-Request Linker computes relatedness by (1) exact correlation ID match, (2) recent trace graph neighbors (within 2 hops), and (3) similar error signatures. Results are ranked and show confidence scores in the hovercard.
Smart Filters are applied client-side for responsiveness; for large result sets we ask backend for a sampled subset and show a banner describing sampling strategy.
To keep the timeline performant we render at 60fps using virtualized spans and collapse adjacent no-op spans under an aggregated placeholder with a count badge.
Design uses semantic color scales: success/neutral/warn/error mapped to existing console tokens. We adjusted red to meet 4.5:1 contrast on contextual chips.
Mobile behavior: canvas collapses lanes into stacked timelines with a persistent correlation toolbar at the top. Editing filters uses a modal on small screens.
Edge case: traces with >1000 spans show a top-of-canvas prompt to switch to a lightweight list view; interactions remain same but timeline is paginated to protect memory.
decisions: Adopt single-canvas pattern with collapsible rails instead of persistent multi-column; reduces horizontal eye movement and improves scan speed.
Show up to 10 related requests inline; for more, provide a link to an expanded related-traces modal to avoid over-populating the canvas.
Implement client-side filter composition for immediacy, backed by a sampled backend query for large datasets to maintain accuracy and performance.
Expose 'Copy correlation id' as a primary quick action because many support workflows require exact copying.
Defer full flame graph visualization to a follow-up; current scope focuses on waterfall timeline and span-level details.
Accessibility: keyboard-first navigation and explicit focus styles required; aria-live region for timeline scrubber updates.
Disabled deep-links to private logs when in private deployments until RBAC checks are confirmed (follow-up security ticket).
